identity.title: Nephrotoxin and contrast exposure history (NSAID, ACEi/ARB, diuretic, aminoglycoside, vancomycin, PPI, iodinated contrast; timing)

technique.how: Reconcile the medication list and administration record for the 2 weeks before the creatinine rise: NSAIDs (including OTC), ACEi/ARB, diuretics, aminoglycosides, vancomycin (with piperacillin-tazobactam), PPIs, and iodinated contrast; record start dates, dose changes, and the interval from exposure to creatinine rise.
technique.prerequisites: Access to outpatient prescriptions, OTC use and imaging history; ask the patient directly about NSAIDs and supplements.

interpretation.positive_finding: A temporally plausible exposure supports a hemodynamic (NSAID/ACEi/diuretic), tubular (aminoglycoside, vancomycin, contrast within 48-72 h) or interstitial (PPI, antibiotics, days-weeks) mechanism and identifies a reversible cause.
interpretation.negative_finding: No exposure makes drug- or contrast-induced AKI unlikely and shifts attention to volume, obstruction and intrinsic renal disease, but multifactorial AKI is common.
interpretation.pitfalls: Temporal association is not causation; contrast-associated AKI incidence is low with modern iso/low-osmolar agents, and stopping ACEi/ARB reflexively is not always indicated. OTC NSAID use is frequently unreported.
interpretation.changes_what: Exposure found: stop or dose-adjust the agent, check drug levels (vancomycin, aminoglycoside) and urine sediment; no exposure: prioritize volume assessment and bladder scan/renal ultrasound.

sources.citation: Khwaja A. KDIGO clinical practice guidelines for acute kidney injury. Nephron Clin Pract 2012;120:c179-c184.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not attribute AKI to a nephrotoxin without excluding obstruction and hypovolemia; do not withhold necessary contrast for a life-threatening indication on the basis of risk alone.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: AKI with a nephrotoxin plus hyperkalemia, acidosis, oliguria or volume overload needs urgent nephrology input regardless of cause.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Medication reconciliation accuracy depends on the sources available; no reliability data for this history item.

extraction_notes: No diagnostic-accuracy study quantifies nephrotoxin/contrast exposure history as a bedside discriminator among AKI etiologies; the item is a guideline-supported risk-stratification and history element (KDIGO 2012 AKI guideline, PMID 22890468 confirmed). Estimates left empty per spec. Interpretation text reflects the guideline's recommendations on drug review, dose adjustment and contrast risk.
